title: Entrepreneurship Is Liberating
primary_theme: Network-driven founder development and sales discipline
secondary_themes: Network capital and early believer alignment
founder_lessons: Invest in founders who treat their network as a real asset and who build relationships before they need them.
Hire salespeople carefully: they can look good in interviews but often require the deepest operational intuition to succeed.
Choose co-founders who can execute through uncertainty and learn from early mistakes rather than launching with the perfect plan.
Mentorship is most valuable when it is personal and based on someone taking a unique interest in you, not just domain expertise.
community_organizations: Brown University Club of Silicon Valley
notable_quotes: I'm so confident they can drop me in Gobi Desert and within three months, I'll be selling something to the locals.
What I really came to realize is selling is very noble. It's like being a doctor... sales is all about listening and analyzing and picking up nuance.
It's all about making the connection. Because at the end of the day, it's your network which is the real asset you have.
